title: Repeat region engineering of Cas13a crRNA enables conformational gating-based autocatalytic CRISPR biosensing.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplementary package (2.88 MB) and extracted all 25 pages of text from the only data-bearing file, gkag893_supplemental_file.pdf. It contains Table S1 (oligonucleotide sequences, ~55 named entries of which ~21 are crRNA scaffold variants plus 7 miR-21 crRNA designs), Tables S2-S4 (spike-recovery results, 3-6 rows each), and Table S5 (a 22-row literature comparison of other CRISPR detection methods). The rest of the package is 16 figure image files (.gif/.webp). I also confirmed via the paper-context tool that the paper reports no accession numbers, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI database links, and no Zenodo/Dryad/Figshare deposit under this DOI.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The data availability statement ('All data supporting the findings of this study are available within the article and its online supplementary information'), the assay protocol details (50 nM crRNA, 50 nM Cas13a, 1 uM FAM-UUUUU-BHQ1 reporter, 37 C for 60 min, read on a Hitachi F-7000 fluorimeter), and the claim of a 2 x 10^6-fold sensitivity gain. I did not see any numeric fluorescence values; every activity measurement in this paper lives inside a plotted figure.

a1_downloadable.note: The supplement downloads freely, but it is a PDF plus figure images only. No machine-readable data file (no csv/tsv/xlsx) was deposited anywhere, and no repository accession exists. Verified by opening the supplementary zip, not from the paper text.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The prediction target would be Cas13a trans-cleavage activity (fluorescence signal) per crRNA variant. It exists only as bar heights and kinetic curves inside figures; it is not a column anywhere in the PDF. The label would have to be reconstructed by digitising plots. Verified by reading all 25 supplementary pages.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present as literal sequences: Table S1 gives the full RNA/DNA sequence of every crRNA variant, blocker and activator, so no identifier lookups are needed. Verified in the PDF.

a4_units_stated.note: Where numbers exist they carry units (fM, pM, U/mL, nM, %, RSD %). But these units attach to the spike-recovery tables, not to any activity label. Verified in Tables S2-S4.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted ~21 distinct crRNA scaffold variants (wild type plus designs a-k, several split into 5'/mid/3' strands) and 7 additional miR-21 crRNA designs in Table S1. The largest numeric table in the whole supplement has 6 rows. The checklist floor is ~1,500 regression rows or ~400 for classification; this is two orders of magnitude short. Counted in the file.

a6_fits_laptop.note: The entire supplement is 2.88 MB zipped. Size is never the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The paper's description of 'multiple DR variants' matches the ~21 variants listed in Table S1; nothing contradicts. There is simply very little to count.

a8_label_provenance.note: Activity labels, where shown in figures, come from a real physical measurement (fluorescence of a cleaved FAM-BHQ1 reporter on a spectrofluorimeter), not from another model. Provenance is clean; availability is the problem. The only model-derived content is AlphaFold 3 structure predictions used for illustration.

existing_models.name: TIGER (convolutional neural network predicting CRISPR-Cas13d guide efficacy, Nature Biotechnology 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on roughly 200,000 RfxCas13d guides including systematic mismatch variants; reported to outperform prior guide-efficacy predictors (exact split and metric not retrieved here).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved - I read the search summary, not the paper.

existing_models.name: DeepCas13 (deep learning predictor of Cas13d on-target guide activity, Nature Communications 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on a screen of over 127,000 RfxCas13d guides; convolutional network using sequence plus predicted secondary structure, reported as the most accurate of seven model types tested.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (an RNA language model) would be the natural backbone for crRNA sequence input
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for ~21 sequences, which is exactly the problem: 21 embeddings cannot train or validate any head.
backbone.licence: Not assessed - moot given the row count.

integration.partner_dataset: Published Cas13 guide-activity screens (the ~127,000-guide RfxCas13d set behind DeepCas13, the ~200,000-guide set behind TIGER)
integration.join_key: No usable key - those screens vary the spacer against RfxCas13d, while this paper varies the direct-repeat scaffold of LwaCas13a under a different assay (purified-protein fluorescence rather than cellular knockdown), so the measurements are not comparable.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: there is no shared identifier or comparable readout linking 21 hand-built scaffold variants to the large spacer-tiling screens.

controls.positive_control: The wild-type crRNA is measured alongside every variant, which would be a natural positive control if the numbers existed.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=21.
controls.external_validation: None - no second dataset measures direct-repeat scaffold variants of LwaCas13a with this readout.

honest_claim_h3: With these files, the only honest claim available is descriptive: 'twenty-one hand-designed Cas13a guide-RNA scaffold variants, their sequences listed, retained or lost activity in one lab's fluorescence assay' - no model trained on this could claim predictive power over new scaffolds.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the sequence of an engineered guide RNA scaffold to predict whether the Cas13a enzyme it loads stays active.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one crRNA (CRISPR guide RNA) variant: its full sequence, plus how its repeat region was rearranged (a loop inserted, or the scaffold split into two or three strands). Only about 21 such variants exist in this paper, verified by counting Table S1.
plain_idea.predict: How much RNA-cutting activity the Cas13a enzyme shows when loaded with that guide, measured as fluorescence released from a cut reporter molecule after 60 minutes at 37 C on a benchtop fluorimeter.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Biosensor developers currently redesign guide scaffolds by trial and error; a predictor would save weeks of bench work per assay. But that only becomes possible with a screen hundreds of times larger than this paper's.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes ~21 crRNA variants. The existing models DeepCas13 and TIGER were trained on roughly 127,000 and 200,000 guides respectively. The one genuinely different thing here - varying the repeat scaffold rather than the spacer - is represented by too few examples to exploit.

confidence_score.why: The spike-recovery tables report n=3 replicates, but the crRNA activity measurements themselves are only shown as plotted bars; no replicate-level numbers are available in any file, so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be estimated.

models_beatable.why: DeepCas13 (2023) and TIGER (2023) are recent convolutional networks with open code trained on six-figure screens. They are not addressing the same variable as this paper, but nothing here provides the data to beat or even extend them.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails every condition: the assays differ (purified-protein fluorescence versus cellular knockdown), the Cas13 ortholog differs (LwaCas13a versus RfxCas13d), the varied region differs (repeat scaffold versus spacer), and there is no join key.

ml_idea: The idea considered was predicting Cas13a trans-cleavage activity from the sequence and topology of an engineered crRNA direct-repeat scaffold, using an RNA language model embedding plus a small regression head, with the eventual aim of designing blocker-gated guide scaffolds in silico. It is a genuinely underexplored question - existing Cas13 guide models all vary the spacer, not the scaffold - but this paper supplies ~21 examples and no numeric activity values, so the idea needs a high-throughput scaffold screen that does not yet exist publicly.

effort.compute_note: Only the 2.88 MB supplementary package was handled; no modelling was costed because there is no table to model. Sizes are measured, not estimated.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in the largest numeric table in the supplement. It is 6 (Table S4). That single count kills the project in under five minutes.

verdict_reason: Fails three Part A killers, all verified by opening the files rather than reading the paper. A1: nothing machine-readable was deposited - the entire 'data' is one 25-page PDF of sequences and a few recovery tables, with no accession or repository entry anywhere. A2: the thing a model would predict, Cas13a cleavage activity per crRNA variant, appears only as bar heights in figures and would have to be reconstructed by digitising plots. A5: about 21 crRNA scaffold variants exist in total, against a floor of ~400. The underlying biology is interesting and the question (does repeat-region topology predict activity?) is not well covered by the existing Cas13 guide models, which all vary the spacer instead - but this is a mechanism paper with a handful of designed constructs, not a dataset.
